buy_title: The kit to order, in the order to buy it
buy_total: The buttons are paid links: as an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases, and it never changes what you pay. Prices in this guide are bands or non-Amazon figures with their source; the button shows today's price.

cards.name: ThermoWorks ThermoPop 2 (instant-read thermometer)
cards.badge: Our first pick · the tool that decides if the turkey is safe
cards.price: Under $50 (about $39 at ThermoWorks, per a search summary on October 6, 2026; we could not open the page)
cards.buy_if: you want the one tool America's Test Kitchen's testers named as the budget pick and the USDA says you need: a real temperature, not a pop-up timer.
cards.skip_if: you will carve and cook a lot all year and want the faster Thermapen ONE, or you already own a good instant-read.
cards.owners: We could not open owner pages this run. Forum posters we saw in search summaries praise the faster Thermapen ONE and report occasional erratic readings after about a year on some units.

buy.pick: ThermoPop 2 (the budget instant-read ATK's testers named).
buy.check: Sold by ThermoWorks or Amazon itself; a genuine unit carries the ThermoWorks name on the body; test it in ice water (32°F) before the big day.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: ThermoWorks Thermapen ONE
cards.badge: The splurge · the fastest reader ATK tested
cards.price: About $100–$125 (list prices differ between sources we saw; check ThermoWorks's own page)
cards.buy_if: you roast, grill and bake all year and will use it weekly.
cards.skip_if: you only cook one big bird a year: the ThermoPop 2 does the same job a couple of seconds slower.
cards.owners: Forum posters in search summaries say the speed and the backlight are worth it; some report flickering screens or failure around a year.

buy.check: Buy from ThermoWorks or Amazon itself; check the warranty terms on ThermoWorks's page before you rely on a number.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Cuisinart MultiClad Pro Triple Ply 16-inch Roasting Pan with Rack
cards.badge: America's Test Kitchen's pick · holds a 19-pound turkey
cards.price: Roughly $100–$200 depending on the store and sale (non-Amazon sources we saw in October 2026; dates unverified)
cards.buy_if: you roast a big bird once a year and want a pan that also makes pan gravy on the stovetop.
cards.skip_if: you cook for four or fewer and a 12–14 inch pan will do, or a disposable pan at $5 is fine.
cards.owners: Retailer-page snippets we saw were positive; we found no owner failure data. Cook's Illustrated reportedly dropped All-Clad over warping.

buy.check: Check the pan fits your oven (width, with the handles) before you order; measure the oven rack gap.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Black+Decker ComfortGrip 9-inch Electric Knife
cards.badge: ATK's electric-knife winner · quiet and cheap
cards.price: Under $50 (a band; the Walmart prices we saw for rival electric knives were $33–$40 in October 2026, dates unverified)
cards.buy_if: you carve for 8 or more and would rather slice skin-on turkey fast than fuss with a chef's knife.
cards.skip_if: you carve once a year for four people: a sharp chef's or slicing knife is enough.
cards.owners: We found no owner data for this model this run. ATK's testers liked it for being the quietest in their test.

buy.check: Check the model number against ATK's pick; the runner-up in the same test was a Hamilton Beach set with a fork and case.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: OXO Good Grips Good Gravy Fat Separator (4-cup)
cards.badge: ATK's fat-separator winner · a $15–25 gravy fixer
cards.price: Under $30 (OXO's 2-cup was about $18 at Walmart per a search summary; dates unverified)
cards.buy_if: you make gravy from pan drippings and hate skimming with a spoon.
cards.skip_if: you make gravy from a packet or a jar.
cards.owners: We found no owner data for this model this run.

buy.check: Measure the drippings first; a 2-cup is small for a 16-pound turkey.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Hamilton Beach Temp Tracker 6-quart Slow Cooker
cards.badge: ATK's slow-cooker pick · frees the oven for the turkey
cards.price: Under $100 (a band; we did not verify current retail prices)
cards.buy_if: you need a side dish to stay hot without taking an oven rack: mashed potatoes, stuffing, green bean casserole.
cards.skip_if: you have a second oven, or you serve sides straight from the stove.
cards.owners: We found no owner data for this model this run.

buy.check: Hold hot food at 140°F or above (USDA's danger zone is 40–140°F).
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Rubbermaid Brilliance Food Storage Containers (10-piece plastic set)
cards.badge: ATK's winner for plastic containers · leftovers sorted
cards.price: About $14–$18 at Target and Walmart for the 10-piece set per search summaries in October 2026 (dates unverified); Costco's 16-piece was reported at $29.99 in store
cards.buy_if: you host and send leftover plates home, or you want a stack of lids that match.
cards.skip_if: you want glass for the microwave and oven: ATK's glass winner is the Rubbermaid Brilliance Glass 9-piece.
cards.owners: Owner snippets we saw say the lids or glass can crack; our research could not open the pages to count how often.

buy.check: Check that the set includes the sizes you need; the lids are the part that wears out first.
